registered_predictions.the_scalar: ratio = bits(best description at a matched score) / bits(the SAME weights under naive per-row uniform quantisation + entropy coding at the same score). This is the one honest number FINDING 12 sec 7b R1 established: at depth 1 width 128 it is 1.13-1.54 across 25 frontier points, median 1.20.
registered_predictions.matched_on: held CE primarily (Logan's standing correction), KL from the model secondarily. Because KL and CE scales differ across cells, the matching level is ALSO expressed as a fraction of each model's own headroom over the unigram floor, so a fixed absolute KL cannot masquerade as a fixed difficulty.

P5_the_trend.prediction: FLAT. The ratio does not grow with model size: the fitted slope of log(ratio) against log(parameters) is indistinguishable from zero (|slope| < 0.05 per e-fold, and the ratio stays inside 1.05-1.6 at every cell). Therefore 'structure does not compress' is a property of the ARCHITECTURE FAMILY as measured here, not an artifact of the smallest cell.
P5_the_trend.mechanism_behind_the_prediction: the conversion law of FINDING 13 sec 6 -- a description whose structure attains R^2 on a table is worth -0.5*log2(1-R^2) bits per weight, and the sparse/low-rank/clustered families spend several times that -- is a per-weight statement with no size in it. Nothing in the family's arithmetic changes with width.
P5_the_trend.the_direction_of_any_residual_trend: if the ratio moves at all, it SHRINKS with width, because the naive baseline's fixed per-row overheads (row scales, histograms) amortise over more columns as width grows, making the denominator stronger; and because the embedding's share of the budget falls from 91% at width 32 to 57% at width 256, moving bits into the body where the structural families do worst
P5_the_trend.falsifier: a monotone increase of the ratio with parameter count, slope > +0.05 per e-fold and > 1.6 at the largest cell -- which would say the negative is a small-model artifact and the programme should scale up

P6_depth_does_nothing_to_compressibility.prediction: at fixed width, depth changes the ratio by less than the seed spread, because depth adds body parameters and the body is the part where every structural family already loses; the depth effect on the ratio is smaller than the width effect

P7_the_structural_only_ratio_is_worse_th.prediction: when the numerator is restricted to descriptions that are made out of an INTERPRETATION (dictionaries, anchors, prototypes/clusters, low rank, feature-conditioned codes) rather than recodings (transform codes, per-column entropy models, stratified precision), the ratio drops below 1.0 at every cell -- i.e. structure LOSES to naive quantisation everywhere, and the >1 headline is carried entirely by recoding
P7_the_structural_only_ratio_is_worse_th.why_it_matters: this is the version of the number that actually answers 'does interpretable structure compress'; the best-of-everything ratio answers 'is fp32 a bad file format'
